reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} but format() only implements YY/YYYY, so lone 'Y' and 'YYY' fall through to the timezone-offset fallback (e.g. '+0000') instead of literal 'Y'/'24Y'; the PR description confirms this exact failure exists before the fix.

After the fix the format regex only matches YYYY|YY, so a single 'Y' stays literal and 'YYY' yields two-digit year plus a literal 'Y' ('24Y'), exactly matching the expectation and avoiding any offset-looking output.

Percent-decoding of route params containing '%' already works at base (the code explicitly calls tryDecodeURIComponent when the param contains '%'), and the PR is only a no-op refactor extracting that check.
The refactored tryDecodeURIComponent keeps the identical '%' check and decode behavior, so '%20' in a path param is still decoded to a space after the change.

At base, reschedule writes the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so the same in-memory entry reports the stale pre-reschedule time; the PR states this regression test fails before the change.
The fix sets @score = at.to_f after the zincrby, so the same entry reference immediately reports the newly requested score and time within tolerance.
Parsing 'Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8' is a long-standing, unrelated capability of ktor-http; the PR only touches Range header parsing, so the behavior is unchanged at base.
The PR modifies only parseRangesSpecifier; Content-Type parsing with charset parameters remains fully functional after the change.

The expected result specifically contrasts against 1-January-1980 zip defaults, suggesting a real known mtime bug in archiving; the attached PR only changes error logging in ComposerRepository and cannot fix it, so the described behavior presumably still fails at this revision.
The PR only touches repository download error messages and is unrelated to zip archiving, so the suspected inconsistent/1980 modification timestamps on re-archiving persist after this change.

The expectation explicitly guards against a JsonException from DeserializeAsync on a large array, which points to a known async deserialization bug; the CredentialCache PR is unrelated to System.Text.Json, so the failure persists at this revision.

The diff only changes URI prefix matching in CredentialCache and cannot affect JSON deserialization, so the async-throws-where-sync-succeeds discrepancy on large payloads with nullable properties remains.

The expectation references avoiding a 'syntax error at or near any' failure, hinting at a real parser limitation with INET operators combined with ANY at this revision; the cursor FETCH fix is unrelated and leaves it unfixed.
The PR only fixes FETCH FIRST on WITH HOLD cursors and does not touch INET/ANY operator parsing, so the suspected syntax error for 'INET >>= ANY (...)' persists after the change.

At base every NO_PROXY entry becomes 'all://*{hostname}', so '::1' yields the unparseable pattern 'all://*::1' which raises when the client builds its proxy mounts, so client construction errors rather than succeeding.
After the fix '::1' is detected as IPv6 and becomes 'all://[::1]', a valid pattern, so the client is created successfully and requests to other hosts work normally.

At base the validation added in the GH#63108 follow-up rejects any regex flag other than re.IGNORECASE (whether via flags= or a compiled pattern), so the DOTALL match call raises instead of returning results.
The fix restores support for non-IGNORECASE flags like DOTALL across flags= and compiled re.Pattern inputs, so 'a\nc' matches and 'ac' does not for both invocation styles.

At base, freezing a chain that contains a mid-chain group followed by more tasks mishandles prev_task/prev_res (issue #8890), so the chain's result tree is malformed and children of the groups are lost or construction raises, breaking the serialization round-trip check.
The fix restores prev_task/prev_res tracking after mid-chain groups, so both parallel groups freeze with correct parents and their four child results survive the as_tuple/reconstruct round-trip.

At base the escape handling intercepts '--' (the current positional lacks allow-hyphen-values) and sets trailing-values mode without honoring the value_terminator, so the first positional swallows '--check' and the second stays empty.

The fix makes the current positional's value_terminator take precedence over entering trailing-values mode, so 'value1 value2' go to the first positional and '--check' is collected by the second without a parse error.

At base the OSC11 handler uses nvim_set_option_value, which after startup fires the OptionSet autocommand (the exact flakiness the PR cites) and the background change also triggers ColorScheme, matching the expectation.
After the change the background update runs under ':noautocmd', which suppresses OptionSet (and ColorScheme) for late OSC11 responses, so neither autocommand fires and the expectation is violated.

Required-field validation flagging omitted mandatory fields as 'can't be blank' is core, long-standing Ecto behavior; the PR only reorders compile-time @derive attribute checks in schema.ex and does not affect changeset validation.
The reordered condition is logically equivalent and only reduces compile-time coupling; required-field validation still marks the changeset invalid with a 'can't be blank' error after the change.
